profile.name: Gustavo Rodriguez
profile.about: Mechanical engineering student working across regulated manufacturing, reliability, robotics, embedded systems, CAD, and human-motion research. I like projects where physical equipment, data, controls, documentation, and the people using the system all have to make sense together.

projects.title: IEEE EXO
projects.description: Project lead for a unilateral lower-limb assistive exoskeleton using AK80-9 actuators, Teensy 4.1 controllers, Jetson Orin Nano compute, IMUs, heel/toe FSRs, CAN planning, and gait-based design inputs. Work includes project direction, technical meetings, budgets, design reviews, procurement, testing, and safety planning.

notes: Lead the multidisciplinary EXO program across mechanical, electrical, controls, R&D, testing, safety, documentation, procurement, and design reviews.
Current hardware direction uses powered hip and knee actuation with a passive ankle concept, with gait-driven torque and timing decisions informing prototype development.
Coordinate board-level events, workshops, recruitment, career-fair and employer outreach, sponsor communication, budgets, purchasing, meeting logistics, and cross-team schedules.
Research work includes Vicon/PKMAS/force-plate data, OpenSim gait comparison, MATLAB analysis, and pre-prototype testing used to support actuator sizing and control strategy.

roles.title: Project Lead / EXO Chair and President
bullets: Lead a multidisciplinary lower-limb exoskeleton program spanning mechanical design, electrical, controls, research, fabrication, testing, and safety; manage design reviews, technical deliverables, procurement, subsystem dependencies, and approximately $5,000 in development budget.

Define requirements for a unilateral hip/knee assistive prototype, including joint alignment, human interfaces, actuator sizing, sensing, power, controls, and test planning; guide integration of AK80-9 actuators, IMUs, encoders, Jetson Orin Nano, and Teensy 4.1 controllers.

Translate biomechanics and motion-analysis goals into engineering decisions on assistance timing, torque targets, prototype architecture, safety limits, and validation strategy while coordinating cross-team milestones and technical documentation.
Coordinate board-level events, workshops, recruitment, career-fair/employer outreach, sponsor and industry communication, purchasing, meeting logistics, and cross-team schedules.
roles.impact: Multidisciplinary technical leadership with approximately $5,000 in development budget.

projects.title: Xcelodose 600S
projects.description: Reliability investigation across failed microbalances and encapsulation equipment using 6M analysis, equipment inspection, manufacturing observation, mechanical alignment, maintenance-history review, comparison across failed units, and corrective documentation.
notes: Reliability: led a root-cause investigation after 3 of 4 Xcelodose microbalance units became unavailable, separating mechanical, handling, static, sensing, communication, and software-related failure pathways.

Applied physical inspection, Gemba observation, equipment history, 6M/FMEA thinking, alignment and corner-load checks, cross-unit comparison, and SOP review to support corrective actions and recurrence-prevention training.
projects.impact: Investigated failure pathways across three unavailable microbalance units.

projects.title: CARRT Research
projects.description: A wearable ESP32/IMU sensor for rugby lineout research, designed for repeatable placement on the ankle and thigh and comparison with Vicon motion capture.

gallery.alt: R9 enclosure: separated housing, electronics, and battery components.
gallery.caption: R9 enclosure: separated housing, electronics, and battery components.

notes: Support human-motion experiments through sensor setup, validation, data collection, post-processing, and data-quality review.
Designed the SolidWorks enclosure around the sensor PCB, balancing a compact footprint with secure strap mounting, protection of the electronics, and access for maintenance.
The early compact housing reduced the footprint from 80 × 60 mm to 48 × 36 mm. It added ventilation and adjustable strap slots so the sensor could mount without athletic tape or a sleeve.
The later battery-integrated configuration measures 62.17 × 58.00 × 16.50 mm. Its larger footprint accommodates the battery, USB-C and switch access, M2 fastening, and service access.

The enclosure revisions balance size with structural integrity: the housing, fastening, and strap interfaces need to hold the assembly securely during movement while allowing the electronics to be accessed. R9 is the assembly shown here.

roles.title: REU Research Assistant
bullets: Support IMU and Vicon motion analysis, experimental setup, sensor validation, and technical documentation.
Develop the enclosure and mounting interfaces for repeatable sensor placement.
Integrate PCB, battery, fasteners, strap mounts, and access openings in a serviceable assembly.
roles.impact: 80 × 60 mm → 48 × 36 mm enclosure footprint, a 64% reduction.

notes: Designed a two-axis carrier and universal spoon saddle around two orthogonal SG90 servos, with a rigid enclosure and a round compliant grip.
The enclosure uses a 108 mm TPU grip and a 148 × 48 × 34 mm rigid enclosure, with tail access for the rocker switch.
The assembly uses 31 mates and preserves two rotational degrees of freedom. CAD clearance checks sampled the four corners of ±25° motion; switch-retention tabs still require a physical fit check.
Next steps: print the enclosure, check hardware fit, implement PID control, and run powered tests.

projects.title: EXO actuator and battery modeling
projects.description: MATLAB modeling to estimate how hip and knee assistance affects actuator current, power demand, and battery requirements.
notes: Built a model that translates hip and knee gait demand into motor current, electrical power, and battery energy requirements for a unilateral exoskeleton.
v1 estimates torque, current, and power throughout the gait cycle. v1.1 explores assistance levels and mission duration to compare battery demand and actuator heating.
The plots show simulated demand. Hardware testing will be used to refine the model’s loads, losses, and operating limits.
projects.summary: Actuator current, power, and battery sizing.

projects.status: Architecture and controller comparison / staged development
notes: Compared gait-event detection, state-machine timing, torque and position profiles, impedance control, and actuator-level control for exoskeleton assistance.
Planned a sensing-to-command architecture using IMUs, foot-contact sensing, and joint feedback for gait estimation, assistance commands, logging, and fault handling.
Defined a build sequence from single-actuator CAN communication and feedback to two-actuator bench testing and integration.
